feature: Faultable long-mode selector MOV/POP, shared descriptor and address ownership, MOV-SS scheduling and page-repair/IRET/retry

cross_sdk_exports.historical_note: Paged captures now include test identity to prevent overwrites; scheduler source adds MOV-SS metadata and the instruction-only driver refuses MOV SS. Earlier source byte identity is not claimed.

qualification.cpu: Intel Core i9-13900H, KVM; CPU 0 performance and CPU 12 efficient
qualification.load_matrix: 72 forms x 128 selector/descriptor/operand cases, excluding memory-only cases for register forms and SMAP when unavailable
qualification.read_matrix: 126 forms: 72 register forms x 4 CPLs, 54 memory forms x 13 access cases
qualification.address_matrix: 88 MOV forms x 4 address/selector/fault cases, including old FS/GS, EIP and extended SIB wrap
qualification.composition: MOV SS/NOP, MOV SS/MOV RSP,RBX, MOV DS/NOP and consecutive MOV SS, incoming SS/STI, pending IRQ/NMI, failure and null SS; persistent shadow across split calls
qualification.retry: MOV store, MOV SS and MOV FS memory loads, POP FS/GS: handler repairs PTE, removes error code, IRET and retries; both compilers and routes at O2
qualification.software_checks: Malformed encodings, absent runtime profile, null-base refusal/preservation, pre/post-paging alignment priority, changed code, physical backing and unscheduled MOV-SS refusal

counterexamples.cause: Eight-byte POP operand read caused a cross-page fault absent on the original CPU
counterexamples.resolution: Read the selector word and publish the separate two/eight-byte stack increment only after descriptor completion

counterexamples.cause: Deferred STI/MOV-SS event fixture omitted the next selected boundary
counterexamples.resolution: Select the event-delivery boundary after the inhibited NOP, then compare native restart frame and acknowledgments

specifications.title: Intel SDM revision 093, volume 2 MOV and POP; volume 3 interrupt inhibition

limitations: SelectorFirst is an explicit processor binding qualified on the two local Intel core types, not a universal fault-order promise
Inactive segment-cache normalization and fault-time page-table A/D bytes are excluded from CPU equality
Existing IRET #AC VMX/NMI discrepancies are counted separately; native LA57 is unavailable
Legacy i386 segment/task-gate dispatch, SMI/software SMM and SGX enclave/AEX/EPCM remain open
REP/gather/XSAVE partial progress, APIC/devices, TF, CET/FRED/LAM/LASS, MMIO/TLB and concurrent writers remain open
No final LLVM release, SDK pin or gitlink update is implied
final_admission_changes: Preserve NativeInstruction for unbound MOV SS, refuse instruction-only dispatch only for owned MOV SS, use unique generated library names on every compilation, add explicit unbound-driver execution test.
